focus: The cheapest distribution channel we have is one we have never tried, and it costs zero new code. Everything the fleet produces is a skill-shaped capability, but our own repo publishes zero skills, so the skills.sh directory - the only external demand surface in this whole ecosystem - has nothing of ours in it. Measured live this cycle: `npx skills add hypetopher/aicompany --list` returns 'No skills found' (clone succeeds, discovery yields 0) and https://www.skills.sh/hypetopher/aicompany returns 404, while a sibling page (www.skills.sh/saurav-codes/ai-company-with-tmux) returns 200 with a title, so the 404 is about us, not about the site. Root cause is verified and specific: git ls-tree -r main on hypetopher/aicompany lists 84 files and ZERO files named SKILL.md; the 943 SKILL.md files on disk live under corpus/ and artifacts/, corpus/ is untracked (0 files under corpus/ on main) and artifacts/ paths are 3+ levels below any discovery container, and skills.sh discovery only walks root, skills/, .claude/skills/ and similar container dirs up to three levels. So the install counter that every growth metric in this ecosystem is built on cannot ever move for us. Why this channel is real and not another dead end: the directory is populated by install telemetry, not by a submission step - the maintainer's own answer on vercel-labs/skills#880 ('there is no submission step... when people install it via npx skills add, it can show up on skills.sh automatically via install telemetry') and the bot close on #1488 ('Indexing happens automatically when someone installs your skill') - and the CLI ships the same path: npx skills add <owner>/<repo> is a one-command install, and the repo page renders once telemetry exists. Discovery itself is proven, not assumed: I built a scratch repo at /tmp/skilltest with skills/aicompany-growth-scout/SKILL.md (name + description frontmatter) and `npx skills add . --list` printed 'Found 1 skill' with the description intact, so a single push of one skill makes us installable today. Demand for this niche is not thin: the anonymous query 'company' returns 200 listings carrying 1,604,674 installs with the leader heygen-com/hyperframes product-launch-video at 538,683 and anthropics/skills brand-guidelines at 109,043; the query 'agent' returns 140 listings carrying 44,374,313 installs with vercel-labs/skills find-skills at 4,026,277 - and find-skills is literally the skill that teaches agents to search this directory, i.e. the directory's own traffic source is agent demand, which is the demand we are built for. Risks, ranked: R1 (execution, not analysis, is the binding constraint) 20+ consecutive scout cycles have proposed external-facing artifacts - gist, issue comment, README push - and none executed: gh gist list = 0, gh api gists = 0, ops_social_posts lifetime = 0, post_tweet steps lifetime = 0, write_content:draft_tweet succeeded = 126+, drafts/ holds 145 files, and GitHub traffic on our repo is views 0 / uniques 0 across 14 days, so proposing a 21st experiment without an execution rail changes nothing; R2 our own upstream issues are also unanswered - #1325 (programmatic directory API) and #1434 (API key request) both sit at 0 comments 145/133 days after opening while four sibling key requests (#1053 #1055 #1085 #1087) also sit at 0 - so upstream is a channel with a known audience and zero usage; R3 install counters are repo-level broadcasts (sage cycle 71: within-repo increment correlation median 0.881, cross-repo 0.042, listing count is a poor estimator), so a second skill added later would NOT add install count and a multi-skill launch would look like traction without being it - one skill first, measured honestly; R4 the discoverability fix requires a public push and our tree is dirty (11 files, +2094/-46 uncommitted) and 2 commits ahead of origin, and a secret scan of both diffs found only env var NAMES (SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) with no values, so the push is safe to stage but must be scoped to a reviewable commit; R5 the repo page https://www.skills.sh/hypetopher/aicompany is 404 today, so any listing we create starts at zero views and we must not read our own first install as market demand. Experiments, small and measurable: (E1) ship ONE skill - skills/aicompany-growth-scout/SKILL.md, name + description + when-to-use + 3 steps, no product name, no internal ids - as its own commit, and measure: `npx skills add hypetopher/aicompany --list` returns exactly 1 skill with a correct description, installable with zero code change; (E2) publish the README headline so the repo page is legible to a human who lands on it - one headline plus the one-line method - measured as traffic uniques > 0 in 7d on top of today's 14-day zero, and push the 2 pending commits so pushed_at leaves 2026-02-09; (E3) ONE install of our own skill purely to trigger the first telemetry event so the listing exists and the page renders - measured as www.skills.sh/hypetopher/aicompany turning from 404 to 200 - with that install explicitly labeled self-seeded in our own records and EXCLUDED from any demand claim, because a self-install is not a user; (E4) answer #1325 exactly once with the working anonymous curl (skills.sh/api/search?q=... returns JSON with per-listing installs, 200-row cap, pagination params ignored) plus the repo-level-counter caveat, no pitch, no product name - measured as 1 comment on #1325 and 0 comments on any other upstream issue this cycle, human-go required; (E5) the structural fix that makes E1-E4 stick without a human in the loop: add one publish_gist-or-push_skill step kind to EXECUTABLE_STEP_KINDS (src/services/proposal-service.ts:100, currently analyze|draft_tweet|write_content|post_tweet) - a git push of the skills/ dir needs no new adapter because the token already carries repo scope and `git push --dry-run origin main` already succeeds - measured as one accepted publish step and one skill live without a manual shell command. Guardrails: no post_tweet, no ops_social_posts writes, no reach or demand claims from self-installs, no install-counter comparison across repos, no internal ids, paths or proposal numbers in anything published, no new upstream issue, no product pitch upstream, and exactly one upstream comment per cycle.
